result.summary: Ensure libbitcoinkernel validation entry points do not mutate or reuse cached validation flags on caller-provided block objects. When invoking `btck_block_check` or `btck_chainstate_manager_process_block`, validation now runs on a shallow copy of the block containing fresh validation state flags while sharing transaction pointers.
result.problem: In the kernel C API, `btck_Block` wraps a shared `CBlock`. Once validation marks `block.fChecked` under one set of consensus parameters (e.g., regtest or a permissive signet challenge), any subsequent check on the same shared block instance bypasses full validation under different parameters, allowing invalid blocks to pass validation or be accepted by a chainstate manager. Additionally, modifying `fChecked` inside `btck_block_check` mutates caller state without holding `cs_main`.
evidence: PR description notes: 'a regtest block fails btck_block_check with mainnet params and ALL flags. After it has been checked once with regtest params, the same call with mainnet params returns 1.'

PR description demonstrates a bug where a signet block valid under an OP_TRUE challenge is connected by a second chainstate manager configured with an OP_RETURN challenge, leaving the second chain unable to read its own tip back via ReadBlock.
PR description reports two new test cases in `test_kernel.cpp` reproducing the issues, which fail on master with four failures and pass with this change.
result.card: Prevents cached block validation flags from persisting across different consensus parameters in the libbitcoinkernel C API. Because `btck_Block` wraps a shared `CBlock`, running block validation caches `fChecked` on the underlying object, causing later checks against different chain parameters (such as testing a regtest block against mainnet rules, or processing blocks across different signet challenges) to erroneously pass. The PR makes `btck_block_check` and `btck_chainstate_manager_process_block` validate against an unfagged copy of the block sharing the transaction pointers. Two reproduction test cases are added in `test_kernel.cpp`.

risk.why: A flaw in block copying or validation flag handling in the kernel API could cause valid blocks to be rejected or invalid blocks to be connected by kernel consumers.
